query:
Research public X posts about building trustworthy, maintainable LLM-assisted
technical/scientific knowledge wikis. The decision is whether exhaustive reading
of all bundled documents/source code should be a prerequisite to a useful wiki,
or whether scoped question/claim-based verification can work. Seek counterexamples,
not agreement. Use actual X search. Return only posts with exact canonical X
status URLs, author, publication date, a concise paraphrase, any linked original
repository/paper, and whether it is first-hand implementation, proposal, measured
evaluation, criticism, or promotion. Do not invent posts, quotes, measurements,
or imply search results represent all users. No verbatim quote over 20 words per
author. Distinguish author claims from verified facts and your inference.
Do not give popularity rankings. If no matching evidence exists, say so.

Find up to 6 original posts by Andrej Karpathy, Steph Ango/kepano and builders of
LLM wikis or scientific documentation about source curation, ingest/query/lint,
human review, and use-driven growth. Check Karpathy status 2039805659525644595
and follow-up 2040470801506541998 if accessible. Include disagreements and
distinguish exhaustive processing of a selected source from all possible sources.
answer:
**No posts from Steph Ango (@kepano) were found that match the criteria** on LLM-assisted wikis, source curation, ingest/query/lint, human review, or use-driven growth (his visible posts focus on Obsidian app features such as web clipper, vault performance with thousands of files, and sync).[[1]](https://x.com/kepano/status/2098428538546421849)[[2]](https://x.com/kepano/status/2093434445093310867)

**Matching posts (up to 6) by Andrej Karpathy and builders/promoters of LLM wikis or related scientific/personal knowledge base tools.** Only actual retrieved posts are included. All are public X posts. Paraphrases are concise; no verbatim text exceeding 20 words is used from any author. Linked repositories are noted only when explicitly referenced in the post. Categories reflect the post's primary nature. Author claims are distinguished from verified facts (none here have independent third-party verification in the results) and analyst inference. The selected posts include counterexamples emphasizing scoped/claim-based approaches or dynamic retrieval over exhaustive pre-processing of all bundled sources. Exhaustive processing of a *curated/selected* set of sources (e.g., a raw/ folder) is distinguished from exhaustive coverage of *all possible* sources in a domain.

**Post 1**  
Canonical URL: https://x.com/karpathy/status/2039805659525644595  
Author: Andrej Karpathy (@karpathy)  
Publication date: April 2, 2026  
Concise paraphrase: Describes ingesting chosen papers, repos, and articles into a raw folder, then using an LLM to compile and maintain a markdown wiki of summaries, concept articles, and backlinks; queries and outputs feed back to grow the base while LLM performs consistency checks. Uses Obsidian for viewing with minimal direct human edits.[[3]](https://x.com/i/status/2039805659525644595)  
Linked original repository/paper: None (mentions Obsidian Web Clipper and plugins).  
Type: first-hand implementation.  
Author claims: LLM handles most wiki maintenance, indexing, and complex Q&A effectively at small scale (~100 articles, ~400K words) without needing advanced RAG; outputs and linting incrementally improve integrity. Verified facts: none independent. Analyst inference: This combines exhaustive LLM processing (summaries and articles for all items in the selected raw/ set) of curated sources with scoped question-driven use and growth; it does not require ingesting or reading all possible sources in a research domain.

**Post 2**  
Canonical URL: https://x.com/karpathy/status/2040470801506541998  
Author: Andrej Karpathy (@karpathy)  
Publication date: April 4, 2026  
Concise paraphrase: Follow-up shares an abstract "idea file" gist so that LLM agents can build and customize personal knowledge base wikis tailored to user needs rather than distributing specific code; invites community adjustments via gist discussions.[[4]](https://x.com/i/status/2040470801506541998)  
Linked original repository/paper: Gist (https://gist.github.com/karpathy/... referenced via t.co link in post).  
Type: proposal.  
Author claims: In the LLM agent era, sharing high-level ideas is more useful than concrete code because agents can implement and adapt them. Verified facts: none independent. Analyst inference: Positions the wiki-building approach as extensible via agentic customization; consistent with the first post's curated-source exhaustive compilation on selected materials rather than all possible sources.

**Post 3**  
Canonical URL: https://x.com/AliAbdaal/status/2041360672379052311  
Author: Ali Abdaal (@AliAbdaal)  
Publication date: April 7, 2026  
Concise paraphrase: Building an LLM-maintained knowledge base inspired by the above that extracts specific claims from raw sources (transcripts, papers, notes) into trust-weighted articles highlighting expert disagreements; applies tiered trust levels with human judgment calls on conflicts while LLM manages structure. Questions how one base can support multiple outputs like books, teaching, and videos.[[5]](https://x.com/AliAbdaal/status/2041360672379052311)  
Linked original repository/paper: None.  
Type: first-hand implementation / proposal.  
Author claims: Surfacing disagreements via claim extraction is more useful than clean summaries; own content and "vetted" sources get higher trust, LLM does bookkeeping. Verified facts: none independent. Analyst inference: This is a counterexample favoring scoped claim-based verification and human review of disagreements over exhaustive reading/summarization of all bundled documents as a prerequisite; it processes selected raw sources but prioritizes targeted evidence and trust-weighting for maintainability and trustworthiness in scientific/technical use.

**Post 4**  
Canonical URL: https://x.com/YoussefHosni951/status/2096299556732596345  
Author: Youssef Hosni (@YoussefHosni951)  
Publication date: September 5, 2026  
Concise paraphrase: Presents open-source LLM Wiki workflow for AI agents that performs parallel research, thesis-driven investigation (gathering evidence for and against a claim before verdict), ingests diverse sources including Git repos and PDFs, and promotes structured concepts into approved projects.[[6]](https://x.com/YoussefHosni951/status/2096299556732596345)  
Linked original repository/paper: Yes (open-source MIT repo linked in thread/reply).  
Type: promotion of implementation.  
Author claims: Moves from rough ideas to approved briefs via structured research, ingestion, compilation, querying, and artifact generation; supports multiple agent runtimes. Verified facts: none independent. Analyst inference: Strong counterexample to exhaustive reading of all bundled documents/source code as prerequisite; explicitly uses scoped, claim-based (thesis-driven with for/against evidence) verification for trustworthy output, distinguishing curated source ingest from processing all possible sources. Supports use-driven growth via project promotion.

**Post 5**  
Canonical URL: https://x.com/femke_plantinga/status/2044798592469405747  
Author: Femke Plantinga (@femke_plantinga)  
Publication date: April 16, 2026  
Concise paraphrase: Contrasts personal LLM-compiled wikis with team knowledge bases, which need verification layers, freshness monitoring, and integrated search; argues pre-mapping all content into maintained graphs is painful and unnecessary because agentic retrieval can build context dynamically on the fly, citing internal benchmark success without stored graphs.[[7]](https://x.com/femke_plantinga/status/2044798592469405747)  
Linked original repository/paper: References article by @Christophepas on Glean benchmark.  
Type: criticism / promotion.  
Author claims: Personal wikis going stale is individual problem; team ones require different mechanisms; organization and pre-computed graphs lose to dynamic agentic approaches. Verified facts: none independent (benchmark is internal). Analyst inference: Direct counterexample and disagreement with exhaustive pre-processing of all bundled sources as prerequisite for maintainable/trustworthy wikis; favors scoped, use-driven dynamic retrieval especially for scientific/team contexts over exhaustive compilation of selected or all sources.

**Post 6**  
Canonical URL: https://x.com/tom_doerr/status/2097247042141601958  
Author: Tom Dörr (@tom_doerr)  
Publication date: September 8, 2026  
Concise paraphrase: Describes LLM Wiki tool that performs multimodal ingestion on PDFs and web clips to build structured personal knowledge bases while extracting images and preserving source traceability.[[8]](https://x.com/tom_doerr/status/2097247042141601958)  
Linked original repository/paper: https://github.com/nashsu/llm_wiki  
Type: promotion.  
Author claims: Focuses on ingestion and traceability in a structured wiki format. Verified facts: none independent. Analyst inference: Supports curated-source ingest for LLM wikis with emphasis on traceability (aiding trustworthiness and human review); does not claim or demonstrate exhaustive reading of all possible sources, aligning with selected-source processing rather than universal exhaustive prerequisite. Related to claim-based workflows in other posts above.

No measured evaluations with external metrics, popularity rankings, or additional posts were included. Search results do not represent all users or all views on X. No posts were invented.
